profiles.meeting_scenario: An enterprise IT team at a multi-building university campus has recently rolled out an SDN controller to manage access switches, building uplinks, and Wi-Fi segmentation policies across the engineering complex. Over the past week, users in the robotics lab have reported intermittent loss of access to an internal simulation cluster and occasional delays when authenticating to shared lab services, especially after moving between wired desks and lab Wi-Fi. The troubleshooting meeting is between the network operations lead and the campus platform engineer to diagnose whether the issue comes from SDN policy updates, endpoint identity handling, or a recent visibility tooling change. The agenda is to review the symptom pattern, identify the most likely root cause, and agree on a near-term fix that can be implemented before the next lab session. The expected outcome is a shared action plan for a 'fix' to the affected segment and a validation approach for confirming that the problem is resolved.

members.name: Priya Raman
members.expertise: Campus networking, VLAN migrations, access control policy operations, incident response
members.background: Priya has managed the university's wired and wireless network for eight years and recently oversaw the operational rollout of an SDN controller to replace many device-by-device ACL changes with centrally pushed intent policies.
members.private_state: Priya wants the issue stabilized before an upcoming robotics competition demo, prefers the least disruptive change to live lab traffic, and is worried that broad controller changes could create side effects in adjacent buildings.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the issue affects the 'robotics lab', they mean the physical lab subnet in Engineering Building 3, not users' mobility sessions outside that room.
A 'policy refresh' is the controller re-publishing the intended ACL and segmentation state to the relevant edge switches without altering endpoint classification logic.
If users can complete authentication and sustain cluster access after a manual reconnect during the same work session, the problem is operationally fixed.
The relevant event window is the one that began after last Thursday's access-switch maintenance in Building 3, because that is when incident tickets noticeably increased.

members.name: Evan Cole
members.expertise: SDN controller internals, identity-based segmentation, telemetry pipelines, automation
members.background: Evan joined from a network automation vendor and now maintains the campus SDN controller, endpoint identity feeds, and the telemetry stack that aggregates flow and policy events for troubleshooting.
members.private_state: Evan wants to avoid reverting recent controller features, suspects the issue is tied to stale endpoint state rather than raw forwarding, and is concerned that the new telemetry view may be causing operators to inspect the wrong evidence.
hidden_assumptions: The 'robotics lab' problem is really a user-identity continuity issue spanning wired and Wi-Fi attachments for robotics users, not a single room's subnet behavior.
A 'policy refresh' means forcing endpoint reclassification and recomputation of host-to-role bindings so the controller rebuilds decisions from current identity state.
A fix only counts if roaming users keep the same intended access without having to disconnect or wait for stale identity entries to expire.
The relevant event window starts with Tuesday's telemetry pipeline cutover, because before that the apparent gap may simply have been hidden by coarser logging.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'robotics lab issue' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the robotics lab issue' as if it is one shared incident.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is thinking of a localized problem on the Engineering Building 3 robotics lab access segment and its associated switches.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan is thinking of a cross-access identity continuity problem affecting robotics users as they move between wired desks and lab Wi-Fi across the complex.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have seen tickets tagged 'robotics lab' and the user reports overlap enough that each can interpret the other's comments as supporting their own incident framing.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that they should try a 'policy refresh' on the affected segment.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means pushing the existing intended access policy again to edge switches so forwarding state and ACL installs are re-synchronized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means forcing endpoint identity reclassification and recomputing policy decisions from the controller's host-role database.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In SDN operations, 'policy refresh' is common shorthand and both actions are plausibly described that way, so the phrase feels specific enough even though it hides two different mechanisms.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the issue being 'fixed'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want to 'stabilize it before tomorrow' and confirm the problem is 'fixed.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya will consider it fixed if affected users can reconnect and work normally for the rest of the lab session, even if the underlying state problem still recurs on later mobility events.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan will consider it fixed only if the identity-to-policy path survives normal roaming between wired and Wi-Fi without manual reconnects or time-based cleanup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using practical operations language about stability, and in a troubleshooting meeting it is natural to assume everyone shares the same success bar unless a formal test plan is explicitly requested.

misalignment_points.topic: Which change window the logs should cover
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss checking 'the logs since the change' and compare before-and-after behavior.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya presupposes 'the change' is last Thursday's Building 3 switch maintenance that altered edge connectivity timing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan presupposes 'the change' is Tuesday's telemetry pipeline cutover that changed how flow and policy events are surfaced in dashboards.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both recently managed relevant changes and each timeline can plausibly explain why the symptom seems newly visible, so references to 'the change' sound mutually understood without either side naming it.
